text:
lena: OrchidCloud flagged a >2x usage discrepancy for March. their portal shows 2.4M gpu-minutes; our charged usage is ~1.1M minutes. they want an explanation before QBR. anyone who owns the marketplace pipeline?

raj: do we have their raw webhook dump? duplicates or missing timezone conversions are common culprits.

lena: they attached a csv and a sample webhook bundle. sample event bundle below (sanitized):

```
[
  {
    "external_id": "orch-evt-111",
    "customer": "orch-999",
    "sku": "ORCH-GPU-A",
    "amount": 1200,
    "unit": "minutes",
    "ts": "2026-03-31T23:59:00-08:00"
  },
  {
    "external_id": "orch-evt-111",
    "customer": "orch-999",
    "sku": "ORCH-GPU-A",
    "amount": 1200,
    "unit": "minutes",
    "ts": "2026-04-01T06:59:00Z"
  }
]
```

emma: two things jump out: same external_id duplicated (retries) and iso timestamps across DST boundary/pst->utc normalized leading to event appearing in two calendar buckets. our dedupe logic keys on external_id+sku, but we normalize external_id prefixes for some partners; possible bug there.

marketplace-bot: Ingestion log: POST /marketplace/webhook orch-999 payload_id=orch-evt-111 status=200 at 2026-03-31T23:59:01-08:00

raj: i traced transformer logs. we canonicalize timestamps to UTC and then apply calendar-day bucketing based on partner timezone (partner metadata). orchid's partner metadata is set to UTC instead of America/Los_Angeles — so the second event after normalization fell into April 1 UTC bucket while partner expected March 31 PST. that explains portal showing both events for March, but why did we see only one recorded?

emma: our dedupe happens in the message queue consumer and uses a hash of (partner_id, external_id) but we accidentally strip dashes from external_id for partners with legacy-normalization=true. orchid was onboarded under that flag. so duplicates with the exact external_id but different timestamp passed dedupe due to inconsistent normalization race.

lena: summary: two root causes: 1) partner timezone misconfigured in partner metadata (UTC vs PST) 2) external_id normalization flag causing inconsistent dedupe for Orchid during retry windows. both compounded, leading to event duplication across calendar buckets.

raj: proposal: short-term: (A) add a safe dedupe pass that checks raw_event_payload hashes across a 24h window for partners with legacy-normalization=true and mark duplicates as ignored; (B) patch Orchid partner timezone to America/Los_Angeles and re-run aggregation for March 29-31.

emma: long-term: remove the legacy-normalization toggle; enforce idempotency at ingress by storing payload_fingerprint alongside external_id. i'll open PR. also add a data-check that flags >1 identical external_id within 2h with differing normalized ids.

marketplace-bot: Scheduled job: reaggregate-window orch-999 2026-03-29..2026-03-31 queued by raj at 1972612700.

lena: good. can we quantify the impact quickly? orchid says 1.3M extra minutes; rough math says duplicates could explain ~1.1M if most events doubled. raj, emma can you run a quick dry-run?

raj: running a dry-run now on analytics: scanning ingress events for partner orch-999 between 2026-03-29 and 2026-04-02 for duplicate external_ids and payload_fingerprint. will post counts in ~30m.

emma: PR for ingress idempotency: https://git.redwood/marketplace/ingest/pulls/614 (adds payload_fingerprint storage + 24h duplicate suppression). includes unit tests and a migration to backfill fingerprint for last 90d.

marketplace-bot: Dry-run job id=197261-dryrun-orch status=running

lena: partner comms: let's be transparent: explain we found duplicate ingests caused by retry handling and timezone mismatch, present exact numbers, and propose a credit for the duplicated portion. cc @legal on wording. mike from acct could you help with credit calc once we have dry-run?

raj: dry-run complete. results: 245,678 events scanned, 112,430 events flagged as duplicates by fingerprint match; net duplicated_minutes=1,180,000. after timezone-bucket fix reaggregation, our March billed minutes will align with Orchid's portal (within rounding). job report: https://analytics.redwood/jobs/197261-dryrun-orch

emma: merged PR to main, deploying a canary now. ingress will suppress duplicates for partners with fingerprint present. also pushing a migration to populate fingerprint for orch-999 to speed up reprocess.

lena: thanks all. action items: raj run production reaggregate during overnight maintenance window, emma monitor canary, i'll draft partner message with numbers and proposed credits. do not send anything until we confirm reaggregate results.

marketplace-bot: Canary deployment completed for ingress v2.1.4 at 2026-04-02T01:20:00Z (canary=10% traffic).

raj: scheduled reaggregate for 1972616800 (off-peak). i'll post final reconciliation csv after job completes.

lena: nice work team. keeping this thread as the canonical recon. :raised_hands:
